label: L18 · Viral Structure & Phage Cycles
rows: Viruses in human disease

OBLIGATE INTRACELLULAR PARASITES. Animal viruses are categorized by NUCLEIC ACID, CAPSID and presence or absence of an ENVELOPE. Most DNA viruses are DOUBLE-STRANDED (some single-stranded); all RNA viruses are single-stranded except the double-stranded reoviruses.
Viral structure
ALL viruses have CAPSIDS (protein coats): HELICAL, ICOSAHEDRAL or COMPLEX (the phage). Genetic material is DNA or RNA. Animal viruses may have an envelope or spikes.
★ The envelope
Obtained during BUDDING of the virus through the CELL MEMBRANE ★; a mechanism to assist in EVADING THE IMMUNE SYSTEM.
Phages and the genome
Phages carry out TRANSDUCTION in bacteria; bacteriophages have bacterial hosts but may impact human health. Replication methods: LYTIC, LYSOGENIC, CHRONIC (filamentous phages).
Lytic cycle

ADSORPTION → PENETRATION (viral LYSOZYME and a TAIL PIN breach the wall and INJECT the DNA) → REPLICATION (normal metabolism turned off; viral factory) → ASSEMBLY → MATURATION → RELEASE (viral lysozyme BURSTS the cell wall).
Lysogenic cycle

Same adsorption and penetration; viral DNA INTEGRATES into the bacterial chromosome as a PROPHAGE; generations of prophage bacteria; a SHOCK induces the prophage to release and start a lytic cycle. May acquire new traits (TOXIN production); IMMUNE TO REINFECTION; SPECIALIZED transduction.
Chronic cycle

FILAMENTOUS phages: flexible rods, SINGLE-STRANDED DNA. NO LYSOZYME: capsid-receptor protein COMPATIBILITY. Virions EXTRUDED WITHOUT LYSIS; host growth SLOWED. COOPERATIVE: the host gains TOXINS and BIOFILMS.
Phages in the gut and immune system

Phages are BACTERIAL STRAIN SPECIFIC; antagonistic or mutualistic; explains the UNPREDICTABILITY of phage therapy trials. Taken in via M cells, epithelial cells, dendritic cells; adaptive response with phage-specific immunoglobulin A and G; T cells make interferon gamma.

label: L18 · Animal Viruses, Kinds of Infection, Onco/Terato
rows: ★ Animal virus versus phage

★ The ENTIRE VIRION is ENGULFED (a phage injects only its DNA); it REQUIRES UNCOATING to release the genetic material (pH of the cytoplasm versus extracellular fluid); RELEASE BY BUDDING, which may assist in acquiring the ENVELOPE.
Non-phage DNA replication

ATTACHMENT → ENTRY and UNCOATING → early TRANSCRIPTION (messenger RNA for “early” proteins) → BIOSYNTHESIS (DNA replicated) → LATE TRANSLATION (capsid proteins) → MATURATION → RELEASE. Most DNA viruses are budded off the NUCLEUS; most RNA viruses multiply in the cytoplasm.
Medical considerations
Viruses are LIMITED TO A PARTICULAR HOST OR CELL TYPE (receptor compatibility); infections range from asymptomatic to life-threatening; many are strictly human, others ZOONOSES carried by vectors.
Course of viral disease

Portal of entry → local replication or spread through the circulation. Common: RASHES, FEVER, MUSCLE ACHES, respiratory involvement, SWOLLEN LYMPH NODES. Interferon, antibodies, natural killer cells and cytotoxic T cells frequently give LIFELONG IMMUNITY.
★ Acute infection
RAPID course; the LYTIC cycle (“acute viral agent”): COLDS, FLU.
★ Persistent chronic
Virus DETECTABLE in tissue, multiplying SLOWLY; symptoms MILD OR ABSENT; may INTEGRATE into the host chromosome: HUMAN IMMUNODEFICIENCY VIRUS, ★ HEPATITIS B VIRUS.
★ Persistent latent
After a lytic cycle, DORMANT: generally NOT DETECTABLE, no symptoms; can REACTIVATE as RECURRENT infections: the HERPESVIRUSES. Viral DNA = EPISOME (in the nucleus, NOT integrated).
Oncogenic viruses
Some PERSISTENT viruses cause CANCER: Epstein-Barr virus → BURKITT’S LYMPHOMA; herpesvirus 8 → KAPOSI’S SARCOMA; hepatitis B → HEPATIC CARCINOMA; papillomaviruses → CERVICAL and PENILE cancer.
★ Teratogenic viruses
CROSS THE PLACENTA → developmental disturbances and PERMANENT DEFECTS: RUBELLA, ★ CYTOMEGALOVIRUS.
Diagnosis of viral disease
Symptoms, ISOLATION IN CELL OR ANIMAL CULTURE, SEROLOGICAL tests for antibodies; some tests for antigens.
Viruses and autoimmunity

A GENETICALLY PREDISPOSED person + environmental exposures → cellular stress and genetic damage; LATENCY and multiple pathogens; viruses DISRUPT EPIGENETIC CONTROL; “fragile sites” on the X CHROMOSOME → AUTOANTIGENS.

label: L18 · DNA Virus Groups & the Poxviruses
rows: DNA virus groups
ENVELOPED double-stranded: POX-, HERPES-, HEPADNAVIRUSES. NONENVELOPED double-stranded: ADENO-, POLYOMA-, PAPILLOMAVIRUSES. NONENVELOPED SINGLE-stranded: PARVOVIRUSES.
★ Poxviruses

Eruptive skin pustules (POCKS) that LEAVE SCARS. LARGEST, most complex animal viruses, LARGEST GENOME; double-stranded DNA. ★ Multiply in the CYTOPLASM, in FACTORY AREAS (most DNA viruses use the nucleus). Specificity for epidermal and subcutaneous cytoplasm → pustules or tumors.
Variolation (background)
Deliberate introduction of smallpox as a preventive measure (NASAL INSUFFLATION); replaced by VACCINATION, a less harmful method. Smallpox REQUIRES A HUMAN HOST; QUARANTINE was the old prevention.
Smallpox: spread, disease

INHALATION of airborne saliva; contact with PUSTULE or SCAB material; FOMITES. High fever, head and body aches, vomiting. Rash starts on the FACE → arms, legs → hands, feet: total body in 24 hours; sores fill with fluid, then SCABS.
★ Smallpox contagion

★ The EARLY RASH (red spots on tongue and mouth releasing virus) is the STAGE OF GREATEST CONTAGION. Contagious until ALL SCABS have FALLEN OFF. VARIOLA MAJOR (toxemia, shock, intravascular coagulation) versus VARIOLA MINOR (less virulent).
★ Eradication
★ The FIRST DISEASE ELIMINATED BY VACCINE; declared eradicated by the World Health Organization. No more routine vaccination except for the front line.
Vaccinia

PREVENTION of smallpox is vaccination with VACCINIA VIRUS: a LIVE virus vaccine, no longer routine; reintroduced for MILITARY and MEDICAL personnel. BIOTERRORISM concern; Strategic National Stockpile.
Molluscum contagiosum

Endemic areas: children. DIRECT CONTACT and FOMITES; in the United States most commonly SEXUALLY transmitted. ATOPIC DERMATITIS a risk factor. SMALL, SMOOTH, WAXY lesions of the genital area and thighs, SELF-LIMITING; TUMOR-LIKE facial growths in acquired immunodeficiency syndrome. Removal of lesions; no vaccine.
Mpox (monkeypox)

Humans susceptible to COWPOX and MONKEYPOX; most cases in AFRICA. Enters through BROKEN SKIN, RESPIRATORY TRACT, MUCOUS MEMBRANES; body fluids, fomites. Fever, aches, SWOLLEN LYMPH NODES → rash from the FACE: macules → papules → vesicles → pustules → scabs. United States 2003 outbreak traced to pet PRAIRIE DOGS.
★ Mpox vaccine
★ VACCINATION AVAILABLE, with a Centers for Disease Control and Prevention VACCINE LOCATOR TOOL. JYNNEOS: a 2-dose series; ACAM2000: single dose, multiple needle pricks.
Cowpox

In RODENTS (the PRIMARY RESERVOIRS), cats, zoo animals; human cases RARE, usually confined to the HANDS; caught HANDLING CATS that met rodents. Re-emerging: loss of herd immunity from smallpox vaccination. A vaccine ONLY FOR ANIMALS (Europe).
Orf virus
A PARAPOX virus of SHEEP and GOATS (sore mouth, scabby mouth, CONTAGIOUS ECTHYMA); humans infected by HANDLING the animals; more serious in the IMMUNOCOMPROMISED.

label: L18 · The Herpesviruses & Herpes Simplex
rows: Herpesviruses

ALL show LATENCY and RECURRENT infection; viral DNA forms an EPISOME. Most people infected, few symptoms; worse with AGE, CHEMOTHERAPY, IMMUNE COMPROMISE; OPPORTUNISTS in acquired immunodeficiency syndrome; may be associated with CANCERS. LARGE, ENVELOPED, ICOSAHEDRAL, double-stranded DNA; replicate in the NUCLEUS.
★ The eight human herpesviruses

★ Herpes simplex 1: FEVER BLISTERS. Herpes simplex 2: GENITAL infections. Varicella zoster: CHICKENPOX and SHINGLES. Cytomegalovirus: SALIVARY GLANDS and VISCERA. Epstein-Barr: LYMPHOID TISSUE, infectious MONONUCLEOSIS. Human herpesviruses 6 and 7: ROSEOLA. Human herpesvirus 8: KAPOSI’S SARCOMA.
★ Herpes simplex: spread

HUMANS the ONLY natural reservoir. DIRECT EXPOSURE TO SECRETIONS; ACTIVE LESIONS the most significant source, but ★ it CAN SPREAD WITHOUT VISIBLE LESIONS: genital herpes transmitted in the ABSENCE of lesions.
Herpes simplex: latency

Multiplies in SENSORY NEURONS → GANGLIA. Type 1: 5th cranial nerve, latent in the TRIGEMINAL GANGLION. Type 2: LUMBOSACRAL spinal nerve trunk ganglia. Recurrence triggered by FEVER, ULTRAVIOLET RADIATION, STRESS, MECHANICAL INJURY.
Herpes simplex 1 diseases

Usually OROPHARYNX, early childhood. HERPES LABIALIS (most common recurrence; itching and tingling before vesicles at the lip’s mucocutaneous junction); GINGIVOSTOMATITIS (young children); KERATITIS (gritty eye); WHITLOW (type 1 or 2, a skin break, one FINGER); GLADIATORUM (wrestling, contact sports); MENINGOENCEPHALITIS (fatal if untreated).
Herpes simplex 2: genital herpes

Usually GENITALIA, possibly oral. Malaise, anorexia, fever, BILATERAL GROIN swelling → CLUSTERS of sensitive VESICLES on genitalia, perineum, buttocks that ULCERATE; urethritis, painful urination, cervicitis. Recurrences usually LESS SEVERE (menstruation, stress, bacterial infection).
Herpes of the newborn

Types 1 and 2; POTENTIALLY FATAL in neonate and fetus; from the MOTHER before or during birth. Mouth, skin, eyes, central nervous system (worst). Prevention: SCREENING pregnant women; CESAREAN SECTION if there is an OUTBREAK at the time of birth.
Herpes simplex: diagnosis

VESICLES and EXUDATE; scrapings from the lesion base show GIANT MULTINUCLEATED CELLS and INCLUSION BODIES (Pap smear); culture; DIRECT FLUORESCENT ANTIBODY tests. Drugs as listed: acyclovir, famciclovir, valacyclovir. Vaccine: none (candidates in trials).

label: L18 · Varicella Zoster, Cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr
rows: Varicella zoster virus
CHICKENPOX and SHINGLES; HUMANS the only natural host. RESPIRATORY DROPLETS and FLUID from active skin lesions. Primary infection = CHICKENPOX; the virus enters NEURONS and stays LATENT.
★ Varicella zoster: contagion
★ MOST INFECTIOUS 24–48 HOURS BEFORE LESIONS develop.
★ Shingles

REACTIVATION → vesicles along DERMATOMES; ganglion inflammation → pain down the nerve; more common in OLDER patients. ★ Shingles patients can infect the UNVACCINATED (especially children), who get CHICKENPOX, NOT shingles. A LIVE ATTENUATED vaccine for chickenpox and shingles.
Cytomegalovirus

GIANT CELLS with NUCLEAR and CYTOPLASMIC INCLUSIONS (salivary gland virus). Saliva, respiratory mucus, BREAST MILK, urine, semen, cervical secretions, TRANSPLANTED tissue. Commonly LATENT in various tissues; evades CD8 T cells (lower major histocompatibility complex class I).
★ Cytomegalovirus: who suffers

MOST infections ASYMPTOMATIC. Virulent in FETUSES, NEWBORNS, IMMUNODEFICIENT adults. ★ TERATOGENIC: newborn enlarged liver and spleen, jaundice, capillary bleeding, MICROCEPHALY; survivors: neurological sequelae, HEARING and visual loss. Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome: RETINITIS. Transplant: pneumonitis, hepatitis.
★ Cytomegalovirus: identification

★ OWL’S EYE effect: an enlarged infected cell, NUCLEUS WITH A LARGE INCLUSION. Microscopy, monoclonal antibodies, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. NO VACCINE: hard without an ANIMAL MODEL. Treatment reserved for the immunocompromised.
Epstein-Barr virus

UBIQUITOUS; infects LYMPHOID TISSUE and SALIVARY GLANDS. DIRECT ORAL CONTACT, SALIVA. COLLEGE-AGE: infectious MONONUCLEOSIS (the kissing disease): SORE THROAT, HIGH FEVER, CERVICAL LYMPHADENOPATHY, SPLENOMEGALY. DORMANT in B CELLS.
Epstein-Barr tumors

BURKITT LYMPHOMA: a B CELL malignancy of the JAW, central African children (with MALARIA coinfection). NASOPHARYNGEAL CARCINOMA: EPITHELIAL, adults, family history, SALT-CURED foods. HAIRY LEUKOPLAKIA in acquired immunodeficiency syndrome. Possible link to CHRONIC FATIGUE SYNDROME.
Epstein-Barr: diagnosis, prevention
LYMPHOCYTOSIS, NEUTROPENIA, LARGE ATYPICAL LYMPHOCYTES; serology for antibodies and antigen. Symptom relief. NO PREVENTIVE VACCINE; therapeutic vaccines for related cancers.

label: L18 · Herpesviruses 6–8 & Hepatitis B
rows: Human herpesvirus 6

Human B-lymphotropic virus. Close contact with SALIVA. ROSEOLA: an acute febrile disease of BABIES: FEVER first, then a FAINT MACULOPAPULAR RASH; self-limited. Adults: mononucleosis-like illness. Over 70% of MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS patients show active virus in lesions; ASSOCIATION (not causation) with Hodgkin’s lymphoma, oral carcinoma, certain T-cell leukemias. No vaccine.
Human herpesvirus 7
CLOSELY RELATED to human herpesvirus 6; similar diseases (ROSEOLA, by saliva); associated with cancers. No vaccine.
★ Human herpesvirus 8

★ KAPOSI’S SARCOMA-associated virus: the common tumor of ACQUIRED IMMUNODEFICIENCY SYNDROME; maybe multiple myeloma, primary effusion lymphoma, Castleman’s disease. SMALL, PAINLESS, DISCOLORED skin LUMPS that may spread to INTERNAL ORGANS. Saliva, sex, transfusion, transplant. No vaccine.
Viral hepatitis
Inflammation of liver cells: HEPATOCYTE NECROSIS; BILIRUBIN accumulates → JAUNDICE. Three principal viruses: HEPATITIS B (DNA), hepatitis A and C (RNA).
Hepadnaviruses
ENVELOPED DNA viruses; DIFFICULT TO CULTURE (DNA injected into HUMAN LIVER CANCER CELLS); UNUSUAL GENOME, both DOUBLE- and SINGLE-STRANDED DNA; TROPISM FOR THE LIVER.
★ Hepatitis B virus

★ Multiplies ONLY in the LIVER, which continuously SEEDS THE BLOOD. MINUTE AMOUNTS of blood or blood products transmit it; also SEXUAL. ★ An issue for HEALTH CARE WORKERS (VERY LOW INFECTIVE DOSE). Can become CHRONIC; raises the risk of HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA.
Hepatitis B disease

Enters through a BREAK IN SKIN or MUCOUS MEMBRANE or INJECTION. MOST: few symptoms, then IMMUNITY. Some: malaise, fever, chills, anorexia, diarrhea; severe: fever, JAUNDICE, RASH, ARTHRITIS (worse with HEPATITIS D). A few: chronic liver disease, NECROSIS and CIRRHOSIS.
Hepatitis B: diagnosis, prevention

SEROLOGY for viral antibodies or antigen (SURFACE ANTIGENS). SCREEN blood, semen, organs, ALL PREGNANT WOMEN. PASSIVE immunization with hepatitis B IMMUNE GLOBULIN after exposure (health care workers, NEONATES of infected mothers). PRIMARY prevention = VACCINATION (yeast-cloned SURFACE ANTIGEN), encouraged for all newborns.

label: L18 · Adeno, Papilloma, Polyoma, Parvo
rows: Adenoviruses

NONENVELOPED double-stranded DNA; ACUTE infection. Infect LYMPHOID tissue, RESPIRATORY and INTESTINAL epithelia, CONJUNCTIVA. ONCOGENIC IN ANIMALS, NOT HUMANS. RESPIRATORY and OCULAR secretions. COLDS, PHARYNGITIS, CONJUNCTIVITIS, keratoconjunctivitis, HEMORRHAGIC CYSTITIS, INFANTILE GASTROENTERITIS.
Adenovirus type 41; vaccine

Type 41: HEPATITIS IN YOUNG CHILDREN (liver enzymes up, jaundice, some liver failure); worst cases show CO-INFECTION with ADENO-ASSOCIATED VIRUS (association only). VACCINE against TYPES 4 and 7 for the MILITARY in training, ORAL.
Papilloma and polyoma viruses
SMALL, NONENVELOPED, double-stranded, CIRCULAR DNA; cause PERSISTENT INFECTIONS and TUMORS.
Human papillomavirus

PAPILLOMA = WART (verruca). COMMON SEED warts (fingers, painless); PLANTAR warts (soles, painful); GENITAL warts (flat bumps to CAULIFLOWER-like masses). DIRECT CONTACT or FOMITES. Nine types raise REPRODUCTIVE CANCER risk. Warts regress but can RECUR. Vaccines: GARDASIL, CERVARIX.
★ Human papillomavirus: early detection
★ EARLY DETECTION: inspection of the genitals; for women a PAP SMEAR to screen for abnormal cervical cells (a KOILOCYTE is the infected cell shown on the Pap smear).
Polyomaviruses: JC virus

Induce tumors in EXPERIMENTAL ANIMALS; most infections asymptomatic or mild. JC: PROGRESSIVE MULTIFOCAL LEUKOENCEPHALOPATHY, uncommon, often fatal; via TONSILS or gut, latent in gut and KIDNEY tubules; CROSSES THE BLOOD-BRAIN BARRIER; IMMUNOSUPPRESSED; destroys MYELIN-producing cells.
Polyomaviruses: BK virus
Cold-like start, then DORMANT in the KIDNEY, ureters and bladder. After RENAL TRANSPLANT and immunosuppressive drugs: HEMATURIA, HEMORRHAGIC CYSTITIS, INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS. No vaccine for humans.
Parvovirus B19

NONENVELOPED, SINGLE-STRANDED DNA; SMALL. ERYTHEMA INFECTIOSUM (FIFTH DISEASE): fever, rash on the CHEEKS (slapped face). Adults: POLYARTHROPATHY (massive joint swelling) or CESSATION OF RED BLOOD CELL production; immunocompromised. Droplet infection.
★ Parvovirus B19 in pregnancy
★ If a PREGNANT woman transmits it to the FETUS: SEVERE FATAL ANEMIA → HYDROPS FETALIS.
Adeno-associated virus
A DEFECTIVE PARVOVIRUS: CANNOT REPLICATE WITHOUT ADENOVIRUS. A VIRAL VECTOR for GENE THERAPY. Not known to cause disease alone; may worsen ADENOVIRUS HEPATITIS as a coinfection.
